title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous page: G is a group scheme over a base S (later a form of SL(2) or GL(2)), and ρ is a section of G. F_ρ is a map (numbered (1) or (3) earlier) that is presumably commutator-like, roughly α ↦ αρα⁻¹ρ⁻¹ up to conventions. A section ξ lies in the image of F_ρ, locally, exactly when ξρ is locally conjugate to ρ. One necessary condition was (4): δ(ξ) is trivial, with δ: G → G_ab. To get computable necessary-and-sufficient criteria, Grothendieck turns to Steinberg's theory for reductive G. There is an invariant scheme I_G, the adjoint quotient G//G, with the canonical map (6) G → I_G. It is universal, compatibly with base change, among morphisms from G to schemes that are invariant under inner automorphisms. So I_G is the 'representable envelope' of the fppf sheaf of conjugacy classes, and there is a map (7) G/int(G) → I_G.

This page makes four claims.
(i) (7) is an fppf epimorphism. Every section of I_G lifts locally to G; for SL2 and GL2 this is clear from companion-matrix (Steinberg) sections.
(ii) (7) is neither an isomorphism nor a monomorphism. Equal invariants are necessary but not sufficient for two sections (here ρ and ξρ) to be locally fppf-conjugate; e.g. 1 and a nontrivial unipotent.
(iii) Sufficiency holds when both sections are regular in Steinberg's sense in every fibre. In modern terms: the regular locus G^reg → I_G is smooth with transitive G-action on fibres. The transporter of two regular sections with equal invariant is a torsor under the smooth commutative regular centralizer, hence has local sections.
(iv) Sufficiency also holds when both sections are fibrewise semisimple.

For groups locally isomorphic to SL(2), probably PGL(2) ('Gp(1)', uncertain), or GL(2), regular means nowhere central. This holds for the ρ of the preceding sections, where the group Γ_∞ = Γ. The page ends by announcing that I_G is well known in these cases. The next page gives I_G ≅ 𝔸¹ via the trace, or 𝔾_m × 𝔸¹ via (det, tr). It deduces a criterion: ξ ∈ Im F_ρ iff (a) ξρ is nowhere central, (b) tr(ξρ) = tr ρ, (c) det(ξρ) = det ρ. That is a trace-coordinate solution of the 'loop equation' ξρ ~ ρ in rank 2.
errors: Claim (iv) is false as stated over a general base. Fibrewise semisimple sections with equal invariants need not be locally conjugate. Counterexample over S = Spec k[ε]/(ε²): take ρ = I and σ = I + εN with N a nonzero nilpotent matrix in sl2. The unique fibre of σ is I, hence semisimple; tr σ = 2 = tr I and det σ = 1. Yet σ is not conjugate to the central element I. The transporter is not flat when the centralizer dimension jumps, so semisimplicity fibre by fibre does not give fppf-local conjugacy. Some flatness, reducedness/normality hypothesis, or constancy of centralizer dimension is needed. The regular case (iii) is fine, because the regular centralizer is smooth of constant dimension.

Claim (iii), regularity suffices, implicitly uses that the centralizer of a regular element is smooth in every characteristic. This is true for SL2 and GL2, which is all that is used, but needs care for general reductive G in bad characteristic.

The epimorphism claim (i) is fine for SL2 and GL2 via companion matrices. In general it follows from smoothness of G^reg → I_G and surjectivity of G^reg onto I_G; it even holds for the étale topology, not just fppf.

ideas.what: Invariant scheme I_G = G//G as the universal conjugation-invariant target, i.e. the representable envelope of the sheaf of conjugacy classes G/int(G)
ideas.modern_name: Adjoint (Chevalley–Steinberg) quotient G//G = Spec O(G)^G; the coarse quotient of the stack G/G
ideas.usually_credited_to: Chevalley, Steinberg (1965), relative version in Geometric Invariant Theory (Mumford) and SGA3-era work
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in SGA3; not in this form in Grothendieck's own texts as far as I know

ideas.what: G/int(G) → I_G is an epimorphism but not a monomorphism; it becomes injective on regular sections (relative Steinberg conjugacy theorem)
ideas.modern_name: Regular centralizer / Kostant–Steinberg section; G^reg → G//G smooth with fibres single orbits
ideas.usually_credited_to: Steinberg 1965 (fields); relative versions by Ngô (Hitchin fibration, 2006–2010), Riche, Bouthier

ideas.what: Using trace/det to decide solvability of ξρ = αρα⁻¹ in forms of SL2/GL2 over a base scheme (criterion on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Trace coordinates on SL2-character varieties; rank-2 conjugacy criterion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fricke–Klein, Horowitz, Procesi; classical for fields

missed.claim: Grothendieck states, in passing, a relative-over-a-base version of Steinberg's theorem: fibrewise-regular sections with equal image in I_G are fppf-locally conjugate. This anticipates the regular-centralizer and universal-centralizer formalism later made standard by Ngô and others. It is folklore today, so this is mainly a historical note.
missed.quote: Mais dans le cas où les deux sections sont régulières au sens de Steinberg (ce qui est une condition sur chaque fibre) la condition est satisfaite.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical precedence only; the result itself is now standard.

missed.claim: The accompanying claim for fibrewise semisimple sections is incorrect over non-reduced bases (and needs flatness hypotheses generally). The thread is left uncorrected.
missed.quote: Elle l'est aussi si les deux sections sont ½ simples
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; shows the draft is provisional ('provisoirement' on the next page).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a solid but standard use of Steinberg's adjoint quotient and regular elements in a relative setting. The relative conjugacy statement for regular sections is now folklore, and the semisimple claim is actually false over non-reduced bases. The setting, the 'loop equation' in the anabelian/Teichmüller context, is interesting but contains nothing absent from the literature.

'[-quasi-] régulières': the struck word looks like 'quasi-' or a similar prefix before 'régulières'; uncertain.
'{+à $Gp(1)$[?]+}': the superscript insertion above 'ou' reads as 'Gp(1)', plausibly Grothendieck's notation for PGL(2) (automorphisms of P¹); uncertain.
'les ρ où la Γ_∞ = Γ des § précédents' — the reading 'où le Γ_∞ = Γ' is plausible; the article is unclear.
